verdicts.reason: A puts the 'Find It Near You' CTA alone at the very top, above the headline, so it is cut off from its copy. Its badges are pushed to the bottom in swapped order, and the cropped green circle collides with the 'Back by demand' pill. B reads in a sensible order (phone, headline, copy, CTA), but in both versions the SOLSTICE wordmark is blown up to full width and moved under the headline, where it competes with it. In B the circle fragment also crashes into the stacked badges at the cramped bottom.

A reads phone, headline, copy, CTA, but SOLSTICE is oversized and placed below the headline, and the leftover circle overlaps the badge stack at the bottom. B moves the CTA to the top, away from its copy, and wraps the headline into a three-line 'back' orphan. It also has the same oversized wordmark, and the badges sit isolated at the bottom on the stray circle.

B is the original landscape layout shrunk into a band in the middle of a tall canvas, with roughly 70% dead space. The copy, badges and CTA are microscopic and unreadable, so it is unusable. A is a real rearrangement, but the CTA floats alone at the top and the headline breaks with an orphaned 'back'. SOLSTICE competes with the headline, and the circle fragment hits the badges.

A crams the headline group against the left edge and puts a large empty gap between the phone and the badges, which sit alone near the bottom on the stray circle. The CTA is also orphaned at the top. B groups the content more tightly (phone, headline, copy, badges), but it has the same CTA-at-top, oversized-SOLSTICE and orphaned-'back' problems, plus the circle collision at the bottom.
